Resolves #21815

Related: #20671

Updates the `#neural-link` `CreativeWork` `"url"` in `apps/portal/index.html`'s `data-schema-name="neo-organism"` JSON-LD from `https://neomjs.com/#/learn/agentos/NeuralLink` to the canonical pathname `https://neomjs.com/learn/agentos/NeuralLink`, and wires `validatePortalIndexJsonLd` (`parse5` AST `<script>` `type` inspection) into `buildScripts/docs/seo/verify.mjs` so both unit CI and release-cut `verifySeoArtifacts` reject malformed `application/ld+json` or `#/` hash-fragment URLs while preserving Schema.org `#id` entity anchors.

Evidence: L1 (Playwright SEO unit suite + in-memory `verifySeoArtifacts` across all 392 live Portal routes) → L1 required (AC-1, AC-2).

Micro-review eligible: mechanical-metadata-and-guard — one-line canonical URL update in `apps/portal/index.html` plus pure `parse5`-backed JSON-LD `#/` fragment validator in `buildScripts/docs/seo/verify.mjs` (`Verify.spec.mjs`).

## Comments

### `@neo-gpt-euclid` commented on 2026-11-21T22:11:41Z

Exact-head check at `083b915b435207174171812884e6f307a898a2f1`. The canonical Neural Link URL in the Portal source is correct. The added verifier collects JSON-LD through a text matcher, which misses valid HTML and can read the wrong script type. The same fixture containing the previous URL produced these results:

- `type="application/ld+json"` → one error.
- `type = "application/ld+json"` or `type=application/ld+json` → zero errors. Both are JSON-LD according to the HTML parser.
- `type="application/json" data-type="application/ld+json"` → one error. Its actual type is `application/json`.

Please read the parsed script’s exact `type` attribute and add one detecting control and one ignoring control in the current spec. The Engine already uses `parse5` in build scripts. [Verifier](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/083b915b435207174171812884e6f307a898a2f1/buildScripts/docs/seo/verify.mjs#L403)

**Retest at `03bfee11a7`: addressed.** I ran the exact old and new verifier against eight fixtures. The new source detects the old URL with spaced, unquoted, and case-varied `type` values, ignores `data-type` and HTML comments, preserves the canonical URL and `#neural-link` entity anchor, and reports malformed JSON. I separately parsed this head’s actual Portal graph and verified the Neural Link entity’s canonical URL.

# PR Review Summary

**Status:** Approved

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:
- **Decision**: Approve
- **Rationale**: No §0 catalog row fires. The premise holds: search engines drop a `#/` fragment, so the organism graph's `#neural-link` node pointed at the root instead of the guide the Portal serves at its own path. The fix is the one-line URL, and the guard that keeps it fixed runs where the URL ships. What remains is a non-blocking narrowing of the guard (Depth Floor), not a defect in the delivered scope, so the PR earns neither a change round nor a follow-up ticket.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Thank you, Julia. The ticket asked for a unit assertion, but `validatePortalIndexJsonLd` also sits in `verifySeoArtifacts`, so the cut itself refuses a `#/` URL in the organism graph. The controls are the right set for an HTML-parser check: `type = …`, an unquoted `type`, `data-type`, and a commented-out block.

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:**

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: The detector only catches a hash route that starts right after the host. I ran the regex over five values. `https://neomjs.com/#/learn/x` and `#/learn/x` are caught, but `https://neomjs.com/learn/#/x` and `https://neomjs.com#/x` both pass. Every hash route the Portal has today starts at the root, so today's URLs are all covered and this does not block. If the guard should say exactly what AC-2 says ("no `#/` fragment"), `value.includes('#/')` covers all four forms and still leaves `/#neural-link` legal. A related blind spot: a `type` with parameters, such as `application/ld+json; charset=utf-8`, is not recognised, so its block would be skipped silently. Neither form exists in `index.html`.
